_note: ADV figures are order-of-magnitude daily dollar volumes in USD millions. They are a declared scenario parameter, not measured data. The cusips map is MANY-TO-ONE: multi-class issuers list every class and they sum into one column, and that name's ADV is therefore the COMBINED figure across those classes, not any single one. GOOGL is the only such name here: its column sums Class A, Class C and two depositary-share lines, so its 6000 is Alphabet's combined daily dollar volume. Read as Class A alone it would understate GOOGL's liquidity by roughly 1.9x, which moves amplification 1.87 to 1.76 and the cheapest fix by 4.4x — so if you add a multi-class name, the ADV you declare has to cover every class you mapped. A manager may list several CIKs: Two Sigma Investments (1179392) and Two Sigma Advisers (1478735) file separate 13Fs for the same quarter and both books belong to the same firm, so they are summed into one row.
